features.purpose: User authentication and authorization. Sign-in, token verification, scopes.

rules: Auth is opt-in: use { auth } from @appdeploy/client only if the app needs user accounts or personalization.
auth.signIn() opens a popup and returns { user, accessToken, expiresIn }. After sign-in, api.* requests auto-attach the Bearer token.
Use auth.isSignedIn() (sync) for conditional UI rendering; use await auth.getUser() to get the current user (auto-refreshes expired tokens).
Handle auth.signIn() errors: 'popup_blocked' (show allow-popups message), 'popup_closed' (user cancelled).
Call auth.signOut() to clear tokens. No manual token handling needed for api.* calls.

Login screen contract:
- Configure the AppDeploy auth popup only in the project-root file appdeploy.auth-login.json. Add or edit it only when the user asks to customize providers, copy, icon, style, or legal links. For existing app updates, inspect and update that exact root file in the app snapshot when changing login behavior.
- Provider selection is controlled by the top-level "methods" array. Supported values are "google", "apple", "x", and "email" (passwordless email link). Omit "methods" or include all four unless the user explicitly asks to restrict providers.
- Valid top-level fields: "template", "methods", "headline", "subtitle", "icon", "style", "termsUrl", "privacyUrl". The only valid styling top-level field is "style"; individual styling keys must be nested inside it.
- Example optional appdeploy.auth-login.json config:
{
  "methods": ["google", "apple", "x", "email"],
  "style": {
    "mode": "light",
    "accentColor": "#2563eb",
    "backgroundColor": "#eff6ff",
    "panelColor": "#ffffff",
    "textColor": "#172554",
    "fontFamily": "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif",
    "borderRadius": 12
  },
  "termsUrl": "public/resources/terms-and-conditions.pdf",
  "privacyUrl": "public/resources/privacy-policy.pdf"
}
- Auth apps should ask for app-owned Terms and Privacy docs or links. If the user does not provide them, deploy anyway; the auth popup renders placeholder legal links until real links/files are supplied.
- Style fields are valid only inside the top-level "style" object. Never put "mode", "accentColor", "backgroundColor", "panelColor", "textColor", "fontFamily", or "borderRadius" at the top level.
- Optional fields inside "style": "mode" ("default", "light", "dark"), "accentColor", "backgroundColor", "panelColor", "textColor" (#RGB or #RRGGBB), "fontFamily", and numeric "borderRadius" from 0 to 24.
// Use SDK auth middleware helpers directly. Do not re-implement requireAuth/withScopes/requireAdminEmailAllowlist in app code.
Use requireAuth() middleware to validate Authorization headers and populate ctx.user.
Use withScopes(...) middleware for scope checks (internally delegates to auth.hasScope).
For admin functionality, use requireAdminEmailAllowlist(ADMIN_EMAILS) and set ADMIN_EMAILS to explicit, real, user-given admin emails.
Auth is opt-in: only use if the app requires user accounts or personalization.
Always scope data access with ctx.user!.userId for protected endpoints to prevent cross-user data leaks.
// IMPORTANT: Scope data access by ctx.user!.userId on protected routes (never return unscoped db.list results).

features.purpose: Push notifications across browsers/devices, including enablement UX, foreground handlers, direct sends, and topic membership.

rules: Use { notifications } from @appdeploy/client for push subscription state, enablement UX, and foreground handlers.
Call notifications.subscribe() only from explicit user action (for example, Subscribe button) when permission is 'default'; never call it from page-load/effect hooks.
If custom prompt UI is needed, use notifications.getEnableGuidance() and call notifications.subscribe({ showUi: false }) from an explicit user gesture handler.
Silent re-registration on load is SDK-managed when permission is 'granted' and user is authenticated; app code should not call notifications.subscribe() from page-load effects.
Use notifications.onMessage(...) for app-specific foreground updates; optionally disable default foreground popup via notifications.configure({ showSystemNotificationOnForeground: false }).
Token lifecycle is platform-managed. App code should not read, list, query, or store raw FCM tokens directly.

Use notifications.send(), notifications.sendToTopic(), notifications.subscribeTopic(), notifications.unsubscribeTopic(), and notifications.listUserTopics() from @appdeploy/sdk for push delivery operations.
Do not implement direct Firebase Admin SDK usage or token storage/query logic in app backend code.
